valid.code: class Base { public static create(this: new (config: { readonly value: string }) => Base, config: { readonly value: string }): unknown { const result: unknown = Reflect.construct(this, [config]); return result; } }
valid.name: the subclass-aware create() pattern with a correctly-typed args array bound to an unknown result is valid

valid.code: class Widget {} declare const widget: unknown; if (widget instanceof Widget) { const value: unknown = Reflect.construct(Widget, []); }
valid.name: constructing a no-argument class with an empty argument array bound to unknown is valid

valid.code: function greet(name: string): string { return name; } const result: unknown = Reflect.apply(greet, undefined, ['world']);
valid.name: applying a function with a correctly-typed argument array bound to unknown is valid

valid.code: function log(message: string): void { return; } function callLog(): unknown { return Reflect.apply(log, undefined, ['hi']); }
valid.name: an any-typed result returned from a function whose own return type is unknown is valid

valid.code: function accept(value: unknown): void { return; } function callAccept(target: (input: string) => void): void { accept(Reflect.apply(target, undefined, ['x'])); }
valid.name: an any-typed result passed to a parameter typed unknown is valid

invalid.code: function greet(name: string): string { return name; } const result: unknown = Reflect.apply(greet, undefined, [42]);
invalid.name: applying a function with a number where its signature declares a string parameter is invalid

invalid.code: class Counter { public constructor(start: number) {} } const value: unknown = Reflect.construct(Counter, ['not-a-number']);
invalid.name: constructing a class with a string where its constructor declares a number parameter is invalid

invalid.code: function greet(name: string): string { return name; } const result = Reflect.apply(greet, undefined, ['world']);
invalid.name: a correctly-typed call whose any-typed result is bound without an unknown annotation is invalid

invalid.code: class Counter { public constructor(start: number) {} } console.log(Reflect.construct(Counter, [1]).toString());
invalid.name: a correctly-typed construct call whose any-typed result is member-accessed directly is invalid

invalid.code: function greet(name: string): string { return name; } function callGreet(): void { Reflect.apply(greet, undefined, [42]); }
invalid.name: a call with both mismatched arguments and an unguarded expression-statement result reports both violations
